clue.text: Go to pieces during analysis

definitions.meaning: to collapse emotionally or mechanically, to fail completely

explanation.surface: Someone cracks up in the middle of a psychoanalysis session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is just a link between the two senses: a collapse, and a statement split into its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a breakdown, and so is an itemised analysis of figures.

clue.text: Garment for the semi-retired?

parts.note: semi-retired is read as half gone to bed, sitting up against the pillows, wearing a short top for warmth

explanation.surface: Which clothes suit someone who has partly stopped working?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi-retired' suggests part-time work; here it means someone who has retired to bed but is still sitting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A short wrap worn over a nightdress while sitting up reading or breakfasting under the covers.

clue.text: Stanza recited in a leaden voice

indicators.note: the letters are spoken within the run of words leaden voice, so they sit inside it

explanation.surface: A verse of poetry is read out in a dull, heavy tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recited in' points at the letters inside 'leadEN VOIce'.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing short stanza of a ballade or similar poem is called by this French-derived term.

clue.text: Bag containing hammer and axe

parts.note: to knap is to strike or chip stones with a hammer, as flint-knappers do
to axe someone is to sack them, dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: A holdall with tools packed inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is a link; the two tool words are verbs here, not objects in the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried on the back is a kind of bag.

clue.text: The right dress, say, for when you're roasting?

definitions.text: The right dress, say, for when you're roasting?

parts.words: The right dress, say, for when you're roasting?
parts.note: roasting suggests a person in hot weather wanting light clothes, but it is food in a hot kitchen cupboard, and the right attire for it sounds like the dishes

explanation.surface: What should one wear when the weather is sweltering?
explanation.walkthrough: 'roasting' tempts you toward summer clothes; it is cooking, and 'say' hints that the clothing words sound like the heatproof dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatproof dishes and casseroles that can go in a hot cooker are called by this collective name.

clue.text: Searching for a boy brought up in Bridgend

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up writes it from the bottom, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a boy is a son

indicators.note: the town name Bridgend is split as Bridg plus end, signalling the final letter of Bridg

explanation.surface: Looking for a lad who was raised in the Welsh town of Bridgend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns SON into NOS; IN is the clue's own word; 'Bridgend' is read as 'Bridg end', the last letter G. Bridgend is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking about inquisitively, like a dog sniffing round, is a way of searching.

clue.text: Frivolous dance of a saucy kind

definitions.meaning: a playful skipping leap or frolic
a pickled flower bud used to make a piquant sauce

explanation.surface: A light-hearted, rather cheeky bit of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' looks like cheeky; it means used in a sauce, as in the sauce served with mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolicking skip is a caper, and pickled caper buds flavour caper sauce.

clue.text: Herbs originally curing nettlerash

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word curing, the one that comes originally

parts.note: nettlerash is urticaria, the itchy skin condition also called hives

explanation.surface: Plants once used as a remedy for an itchy rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' picks the C of 'curing'.
explanation.definitionFit: These slender onion-flavoured leaves are a common kitchen herb.

clue.text: Left sheet of paper in case

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
a folio is a single leaf or sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A page was left behind in a briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat carrying case for loose papers or drawings.

clue.text: Fight off untouchable's promotion

indicators.note: promotion moves something upward, and in a down clue an upward word reads backwards

parts.note: a leper is someone shunned and never touched; the possessive 's is a link

explanation.surface: Resisting the rise of a member of India's lowest caste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' lifts LEPER, reversing it in this down clue. 'Untouchable' suggests the Indian caste; here it is an outcast with leprosy.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to drive it back.

clue.text: Turn aside from French production of "Evita"

parts.note: de is the French word for from

indicators.note: a staging of the musical rearranges its title letters, a fresh production of them

explanation.surface: Departing from the French staging of the musical Evita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges EVITA to make VIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to stray from a course.

clue.text: Agitate about the king and put your foot in it

parts.note: to stir is to agitate
R is short for rex, Latin for king
up as in up and about, out of bed and active

explanation.surface: Stir things up around the monarch and then make a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put your foot in it' looks like the idiom for a gaffe; read literally it describes the rider's foot rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot rests in the metal loop hanging from a saddle.

clue.text: Someone's second name

parts.note: not a middle name but an assumed one, the other name a person goes by

explanation.surface: A question about a person's middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second name' suggests a surname or middle name; it is a false name used besides one's real one.
explanation.definitionFit: A false identity or assumed name used in place of one's own.

clue.text: Ace flew round eruption

indicators.note: an eruption scatters material violently, so the letters of flew round are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot circled a volcano as it blew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' looks like a flying ace, which suits the pilot picture; it is the slang adjective meaning excellent, and 'eruption' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace as slang adjective means excellent, superb.

clue.text: Circular lock needing light touch and a twist

parts.note: a kiss is a gentle touch, as of a ball grazing another in billiards
a curl is a twist or coil

explanation.surface: A round lock that opens with a gentle touch and a turn of the key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door lock opened by a twist; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat curl of hair pressed against the forehead or cheek.

clue.text: Curious case about the place of a food additive

definitions.text: the place of a food additive

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters of case about are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: A strange court case concerning where a food additive comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges CASE ABOUT. 'food additive' sounds like a chemical; it is gravy or sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat-shaped jug is where gravy or other pouring sauce is kept at the table.

clue.text: Pitch mark players must attend to

definitions.text: Pitch mark players must attend to

parts.words: Pitch mark players must attend to
parts.note: pitch and players suggest a sports field; read as musicians reading a symbol that fixes the pitch of the stave

explanation.surface: A dent on the cricket ground that the team should repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' and 'players' suggest sport; the players are musicians and pitch is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The sign at the start of a stave fixing which notes the lines stand for.

clue.text: One of the brothers has to rescue mother and boy

parts.note: to rescue is to free
ma is a familiar word for mother
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A monk must save his mother and her child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brothers' suggests monks or siblings; it is members of a fraternal secret society.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the fraternal Masonic order call one another brother.

clue.text: Top of battery has corroded and is dilapidated

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: corroded means eaten away, eaten up

explanation.surface: The top of a car battery has rusted and is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of' picks the B of 'battery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered and decrepit, as a worn-out old car is.

clue.text: Clothing that makes valets curse

parts.note: valets are manservants, men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Garments so awful that the servants who look after them swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that makes' is a link: the pieces make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes made for male customers, as in a department store section.

clue.text: Tense explained in reported speech

indicators.note: reported speech here means spoken aloud, so the word is said and heard

parts.note: to have explained something is to have taught it

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on verb tenses in indirect speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' and 'reported speech' suggest grammar; tense means tight, and the phrase marks a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretched tight, as a rope or nerves can be.

clue.text: The girl to go off with on a swan

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
to elope is to go off with a lover secretly

explanation.surface: A young woman runs away riding on a swan, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is an across-clue placing signal: the escaping piece sits after the bird. 'swan' here means specifically a female one.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, borne by the faithful wife of Odysseus.

clue.text: Church attracting mischievous children — the monkeys!

parts.note: imps are naughty children

explanation.surface: The church draws in naughty kids, little monkeys that they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkeys' suggests the playful term for naughty children; it is literal apes.
explanation.definitionFit: These African apes are relatives of monkeys loosely so called.

clue.text: By degrees contraction is apparent in the cement

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree, so two or more are MAs
a tic is an involuntary muscle contraction

explanation.surface: Shrinkage that shows only gradually in setting concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' looks like 'gradually'; here 'degrees' is university qualifications, 'By' and 'is apparent in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin-based putty or mortar used as an adhesive filler.

clue.text: Kind of surgery one finds in a public centre

parts.note: open means public, as in an open meeting
the heart is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A doctor's practice found in the middle of a busy area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one finds in a' is a link between the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations where the chest is opened and the cardiac organ exposed.

clue.text: Look up and study antique

indicators.note: in a down clue the word goes up, so it is written backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Research and examine an old item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LO to OL. 'Look up and study' reads like research.
explanation.definitionFit: Of times long past, ancient.

clue.text: At first such a genial host

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word such

parts.note: genial means warm and friendly

explanation.surface: A welcoming party host greets guests warmly at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like the person entertaining; it means a great crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A host, in the old sense of a multitude, is a teeming crowd.

clue.text: A wide range of maps

definitions.meaning: the mountain range in north Africa

explanation.surface: A broad selection of charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'range' is read as mountains rather than a selection.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African mountain chain shares its name with a bound collection of charts.

clue.text: The passive sort that gets trodden on

definitions.text: The passive sort that gets trodden on

parts.words: The passive sort that gets trodden on
parts.note: describes a meek person walked over by others, and also the mat at the threshold wiped by shoes

explanation.surface: A meek person whom everyone walks all over.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings point the same way: a submissive person, and the thing literally underfoot at an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A meek person who lets others exploit them is likened to the mat wiped by shoes.

clue.text: Leaves the rocks

definitions.meaning: the thin pointed foliage of pines and firs
a row of chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of the stony place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb meaning departs; it is the noun. The Needles are chalk stacks off England's Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine leaves are slender spikes, and the chalk stacks at the Isle of Wight share the name.

clue.text: Music makers determined to make a come-back

indicators.note: making a come-back is going back the way one came, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: set on means determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: Musicians resolved to return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a come-back' reverses SET ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Individual sounds or written symbols are what music is made from.

clue.text: Rich dressing a knight upset when stuffing a fowl

indicators.note: stuffing puts something inside a bird, so these letters go inside the fowl

parts.note: a capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the title for a knight is written backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is annoyed by the lavish sauce served with stuffed poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SIR into RIS; 'stuffing' puts A RIS into CAPON. 'dressing' suggests salad or stuffing; it is a horse's ornamental cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornate decorative cloth covering a horse, a rich trapping.
